title: Connect Cisco Meraki to Micetro with an API Key

cta.text: See Micetro with your Meraki estate

prompt:
Product: BlueCat. Demo: "Connect Cisco Meraki to Micetro with an API Key".
Story: Connect Cisco Meraki to Micetro in One Wizard
Your Meraki branches already hold the networks, VLANs and clients you need to manage. Watch BlueCat Micetro connect to them with a single API key, with no appliance at any branch. About 3 minutes.
Audience: network and DNS engineers and IT leaders evaluating the product. Tone: concise, confident, practical, no hype.
10 screenshots, keep this order, one tooltip per image, calling out the highlighted UI element:
1. Meraki is a built-in service type.
2. Cisco Meraki, listed with the other DHCP and IPAM providers.
3. A Micetro DHCP agent proxies the calls to Meraki. The central host works out of the box.
4. Give the service a name you will recognise.
5. Connect with a Meraki API key. That is the whole credential, and it stays masked.
6. You can list organization or network IDs to skip, one per line. Here we sync everything.
7. Review the summary. The key is not shown.
8. Add a change comment.
9. The service is added and the first sync starts.
10. The branch networks appear in the same pane as everything else, with no change to your Meraki setup and no appliance at each branch.
Close: One API key, and every Meraki network appears next to the rest of your IP space.
End with a call to action: See Micetro with your Meraki estate.
